key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings with more disk-like, well-spread droplets form denser microstructures and show better long-term corrosion and wear performance, especially in humid environments.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters to minimize porosity can improve the durability of carbon-steel protection coatings in corrosive and tribologically active service conditions.
method: Fe-based amorphous coatings were deposited on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under different parameters.
Coating morphology/microstructure was assessed through droplet spreading characteristics and defect/porosity levels.
Corrosion and tribology tests were performed across different humidity environments.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic testing showing that higher porosity lowers long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces both friction coefficient and wear rate.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on deposition quality and environmental humidity, so results may not directly transfer to other substrates, spray settings, or service conditions without re-optimization.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
